prompt:
Redraw this typing-trainer app screen with a NEW LAYOUT while keeping the exact visual identity of the reference image: the same quiet dark charcoal ground (#2B2D31), the same monospace type, the same single mustard yellow accent, the same soft pink / yellow / green / blue finger colours, the same softly rounded dark keys, the same restraint. Flat-on desktop UI design comp, 3:2 landscape, no browser chrome. Finish level of a premium dark product tool: tight spacing, hairline dividers at very low contrast, crisp small type.

New layout, a three-zone cockpit that uses the full width:

1. Top strip, unchanged in content: far left the lowercase mustard wordmark auriculaire; then five small lowercase tabs: highway, words, pairs, anchors, stats, with highway light and the others muted; far right a small dropdown reading colemak-dh and a toggle fr / en.

2. Left rail, about 22 percent of the width, left-aligned text: the numeral 87 in mustard yellow, very large (about one fifth of the screen height), with the small caption wpm · rolling 10 s under it. Under that a thin muted sparkline of the last minute. Then two small rows: acc 96% and streak 41. Then a small block titled fingers with four thin horizontal bars labelled pinky, ring, middle, index, drawn in pink, yellow, green and blue; the pinky bar is the shortest and the index bar the longest.

3. Centre, about 50 percent of the width, running the full height under the top strip: the falling-notes highway, tall. Eight vertical lanes in two groups of four with a gap between the groups, separated by faint grey lines. Only ten notes in total, sparse, at different heights: outermost lanes (pinky) carry pink diamonds, next lanes (ring) yellow triangles, next (middle) green squares, innermost lanes (index) blue circles, each holding ONE lowercase monospace letter in dark charcoal: q, a, p, o, l, s, w, e, n, t. A thin light grey strike line. Directly under the strike line and exactly as wide as the eight lanes: the keyboard, three letter rows plus a space bar, keys softly tinted by finger zone, the eight home-row keys aligned exactly under the eight lanes. The next key p, top row on the right pinky side, is bright pink.

4. Right rail, about 22 percent of the width: two large hand outlines seen from above in muted grey line, fingers pointing up, about a third of the screen height, each fingertip marked by a small dot in its finger colour; the right pinky is filled solid pink. Under the hands a small label next key, then one large rounded key cap in pink showing the letter p, and the caption right pinky.

Rules: no gradients, no glow, no cards, no boxes around the rails; the three zones are separated only by empty space. Generous margins. Everything aligned to a calm grid.
